subject: Chemistry
title: Gas vs. Aqueous Phase Basicity Trends & The Aniline Ortho-Effect
topics: 2. Amine Basicity Principles (pK_b = -log K_b, smaller pK_b = stronger base)
Factors Governing Aqueous Basicity: +I Inductive Effect, Hydration Energy, and Steric Hindrance
2.1 Basicity Trends Matrix: Gas Phase (3° > 2° > 1° > NH₃) vs Aqueous Phase
Aqueous Methyl Substituted Order: (CH₃)₂NH (2°) > CH₃NH₂ (1°) > (CH₃)₃N (3°) > NH₃ (Order: 213)
Aqueous Ethyl Substituted Order: (C₂H₅)₂NH (2°) > (C₂H₅)₃N (3°) > C₂H₅NH₂ (1°) > NH₃ (Order: 231)
2.2 Aniline Resonance Delocalization (pK_b = 9.38 vs 4.75 for NH₃) & The Aniline Ortho-Effect
quickSummary: Gas phase basicity follows pure +I effect: 3° > 2° > 1° > NH₃. Aqueous basicity balances +I, hydration, and sterics: Methyl order is 2° > 1° > 3° > NH₃ (213); Ethyl order is 2° > 3° > 1° > NH₃ (231). Aniline (pK_b = 9.38) is 10⁶x weaker than NH₃ because its lone pair delocalizes across 5 canonical structures. The Ortho-Effect makes almost all o-substituted anilines weaker bases than aniline.
summary: Master gas-phase and aqueous basicity hierarchies, aniline resonance deactivation, and the aniline ortho-effect.

summaryBox.title: Basicity Mnemonic Orders
summaryBox.takeaway: Gas Phase: 3° > 2° > 1° > NH₃ (pure +I). Aqueous Methyl: 2° > 1° > 3° > NH₃ (213). Aqueous Ethyl: 2° > 3° > 1° > NH₃ (231).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
GAS PHASE BASICITY (Pure $+I$ Effect Dominates)
                 
                 $$\mathbf{3^\circ \text{ Amine } (R_3N) > 2^\circ \text{ Amine } (R_2NH) > 1^\circ \text{ Amine } (RNH_2) > NH_3}$$

               AQUEOUS PHASE BASICITY (Interplay of $+I$, Hydration, & Sterics)
               
   For Methyl Substitution ($R = -\text{CH}_3$):       $$\mathbf{(CH_3)_2NH \ (2^\circ) > CH_3NH_2 \ (1^\circ) > (CH_3)_3N \ (3^\circ) > NH_3 \quad (\text{Order: } 213)}$$
   For Ethyl Substitution ($R = -\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$):    $$\mathbf{(C_2H_5)_2NH \ (2^\circ) > (C_2H_5)_3N \ (3^\circ) > C_2H_5NH_2 \ (1^\circ) > NH_3 \quad (\text{Order: } 231)}$$
conceptBreakdown.content: Amines are basic due to nitrogen's lone pair. In the gas phase, $+I$ electron donation completely determines stability ($3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ > 	ext{NH}_3$). In aqueous solution, solvation by hydrogen bonding ($	ext{RNH}_3^+ > 	ext{R}_2	ext{NH}_2^+ > 	ext{R}_3	ext{NH}^+$) and steric hindrance combine with $+I$ to yield the classic 213 (methyl) and 231 (ethyl) orders.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ANILINE RESONANCE DELOCALIZATION
                      
   :NH₂               NH₂⁺               NH₂⁺               NH₂⁺
    │                  ║                  ║                  ║
   / \   ────────►    / \⁻   ────────►   / \    ────────►   /⁻ \
  |   |              |   |              |⁻  |              |   |
   \ /                \ /                \ /                \ /

• Aniline (pKb = 9.38) is 10⁶x WEAKER than NH₃ (pKb = 4.75) due to 5 canonical resonance forms.
• Ortho-Effect in Anilines: Almost ALL o-substituted anilines are WEAKER BASES than Aniline!
  Basicity Order: p-Toluidine > m-Toluidine > Aniline > o-Toluidine
  Nitroaniline Order: p-Nitroaniline > m-Nitroaniline > Aniline > o-Nitroaniline
conceptBreakdown.content: Aniline is a weak base because its lone pair is delocalized into the ring. Substituents modulate basicity ($+M/+I$ increase basicity; $-M/-I$ decrease basicity). In the *ortho* position, steric hindrance to protonation and loss of coplanarity make *ortho*-substituted anilines weaker bases than aniline.
